claim: People living with obesity have elevated levels of the peptide hormone leptin.
source: People living with obesity have elevated levels of the peptide hormone leptin.
evidence: Supported by citation to Obradovic et al., 2021

claim: The amount of leptin in circulation is proportional to the amount of adipose tissue that an individual has.
source: This can be attributed to the amount of leptin in circulation being proportional to the amount of adipose tissue that an individual has (Obradovic et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Obradovic et al., 2021

claim: Leptin is secreted by fat cells in adipose tissue.
source: After being secreted by fat cells in adipose tissue, leptin predominantly acts in the hypothalamus as a major regulator of energy balance (Morrison, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Morrison, 2009

claim: Leptin predominantly acts in the hypothalamus as a major regulator of energy balance.
source: After being secreted by fat cells in adipose tissue, leptin predominantly acts in the hypothalamus as a major regulator of energy balance (Morrison, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Morrison, 2009

claim: Both neural and adipose tissues play an important role in the molecular etiology of body mass index (BMI).
source: Likewise, both neural and adipose tissues are known to play an important role in the molecular etiology of body mass index (BMI), which is conventionally used to clinically diagnose obesity.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field

claim: BMI is conventionally used to clinically diagnose obesity.
source: Likewise, both neural and adipose tissues are known to play an important role in the molecular etiology of body mass index (BMI), which is conventionally used to clinically diagnose obesity.
evidence: Stated as established clinical practice

claim: BMI is a construct that captures multiple heterogeneous subcomponents.
source: However, despite being a cost-effective approach to routinely measure adiposity at scale, BMI is a construct that captures multiple heterogeneous subcomponents.
evidence: Supported by subsequent citations to functional gene studies

claim: Functional genes exert their effects on adiposity via their expression in brain and adipose tissues.
source: This is epitomized by previous investigations into the functional genes that exert their effects on adiposity via their expression in brain and adipose tissues (Timshel et al., 2020; Rask-Andersen et al., 2019), highlighting the divergent pathways that exist between BMI and downstream complex traits.
evidence: Supported by citations to Timshel et al., 2020 and Rask-Andersen et al., 2019

claim: Divergent pathways exist between BMI and downstream complex traits.
source: This is epitomized by previous investigations into the functional genes that exert their effects on adiposity via their expression in brain and adipose tissues (Timshel et al., 2020; Rask-Andersen et al., 2019), highlighting the divergent pathways that exist between BMI and downstream complex traits.
evidence: Inferred from cited studies on functional genes

claim: Brain-derived BMI variants are predominantly responsible for driving the effect of BMI on cardiometabolic disease outcomes.
source: Using this approach suggested that the brain-derived variants are predominantly responsible for driving the effect of BMI on cardiometabolic disease outcomes (Leyden et al., 2022), which we postulate is due to their involvement in appetite regulation and energy expenditure.
evidence: Supported by citation to Leyden et al., 2022

claim: Brain-derived BMI variants' effects on cardiometabolic disease outcomes are due to their involvement in appetite regulation and energy expenditure.
source: Using this approach suggested that the brain-derived variants are predominantly responsible for driving the effect of BMI on cardiometabolic disease outcomes (Leyden et al., 2022), which we postulate is due to their involvement in appetite regulation and energy expenditure.
evidence: Authors' postulation based on previous findings

claim: SAT-derived BMI instruments are predominantly responsible for the effect of BMI on endometrial cancer.
source: Conversely, the SAT-derived set of instruments were predominantly responsible for the effect of BMI on outcomes such as endometrial cancer (Leyden et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Leyden et al., 2023

claim: Associations between BMI and leptin levels have been reported as early in life as childhood.
source: However, investigating this hypothesis is made even more challenging given that associations between BMI and leptin levels have been reported as early in life as childhood (Shalitin and Phillip, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shalitin and Phillip, 2003

claim: Genetic instruments for childhood and adult adiposity can separate clinically measured childhood and adult BMI in three independent cohorts.
source: Briefly, genetic instruments derived in the UK Biobank study based on self-reported body size at age 10 and measured adulthood BMI (Richardson et al., 2020) have been shown to separate clinically measured childhood and adult BMI in three independent cohorts (Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children [ALSPAC] [Richardson et al., 2020], the Young Finns Study [Richardson et al., 2021], and the Trøndelag Health (HUNT) study [Brandkvist et al., 2021]).
evidence: Supported by citations to Richardson et al., 2020, Richardson et al., 2021, and Brandkvist et al., 2021

claim: 86 independent adult BMI-associated instruments provided evidence of sharing a causal variant with proximal gene expression in subcutaneous adipose tissue through genetic colocalization analyses (based on a posterior probability [PPA] > 0.8).
source: In brief, 86 independent adult BMI-associated instruments provided evidence of sharing a causal variant with proximal gene expression in subcutaneous adipose tissue through genetic colocalization analyses (based on a posterior probability [PPA] > 0.8).
evidence: Data from previous methodology described in Leyden et al., 2022

claim: 140 adult BMI instruments have effects putatively mediated by a nearby gene's expression in brain tissue.
source: The same approach provided evidence that the effects of 140 adult BMI instruments are putatively mediated by a nearby gene's expression in brain tissue.
evidence: Data from previous methodology described in Leyden et al., 2022

claim: Adipose tissue-derived and brain tissue-derived BMI instruments have near identical average effect sizes on BMI (adipose = 0.0148 and brain = 0.0149 standard deviation change in BMI per effect allele).
source: These two sets of genetic variants have near identical average effect sizes on BMI (adipose = 0.0148 and brain = 0.0149 standard deviation [SD] change in BMI per effect allele), although the manner in which they relate to other anthropometric traits can markedly differ.
evidence: Data from previous study

claim: Brain tissue BMI instruments are more strongly correlated with waist-to-hip ratio compared to adipose tissue instruments (r = 0.733 and r = 0.445, respectively, pcomparison=0.001).
source: For instance, we previously found that the brain tissue instruments were more strongly correlated with waist-to-hip ratio compared to the adipose–tissue instruments (r = 0.733 and r = 0.445, respectively, pcomparison=0.001).
evidence: Data from previous study

claim: Brain tissue BMI instruments are more highly correlated with visceral adipose tissue than adipose tissue instruments (r = 0.554 and r = 0.254, respectively, pcomparison=0.009).
source: Likewise, the brain tissue set was more highly correlated than the adipose set with a measure of visceral adipose tissue from the UK Biobank study (r = 0.554 and r = 0.254, respectively, pcomparison=0.009), further suggesting that the way in which these tissue-partitioned sets of variants exert their effects on BMI likely varies in terms of biological pathways.
evidence: Data from previous study

claim: Childhood leptin levels were measured from non-fasting blood samples taken from ALSPAC participants at mean age 9.9 y (range = 8.9–11.5 y).
source: Childhood measures of circulating leptin levels were obtained from non-fasting blood samples taken from ALSPAC participants at mean age 9.9 y (range = 8.9–11.5 y).
evidence: Description of data collection methods

claim: Leptin was measured by an in-house ELISA validated against commercial methods.
source: Leptin was measured by an in-house ELISA validated against commercial methods.
evidence: Description of measurement methodology

claim: Analyses in ALSPAC were undertaken on a final sample size of 4155 individuals after removing those without genetic data and withdrawn consent.
source: Analyses in ALSPAC were undertaken on a final sample size of 4155 individuals after removing those without genetic data and withdrawn consent.
evidence: Description of study sample

claim: Genetic estimates on adulthood circulating leptin levels were obtained from a study of 10,708 individuals enrolled in the Fenland study.
source: Genetic estimates on adulthood circulating leptin levels were obtained from a study of 10,708 individuals enrolled in the Fenland study.
evidence: Description of data source

claim: Leptin was measured using the SomaScan v4 assay in the Fenland study.
source: Leptin was measured using the SomaScan v4 assay, which applies single-stranded oligonucleotides aptamers with specific binding affinities to protein targets.
evidence: Description of measurement methodology

claim: The SomaScan assay provides a very highly correlated measure of circulating leptin with the antibody-based Olink platform (r = 0.95).
source: This assay has also been reported to provide a very highly correlated measure of circulating leptin using the antibody-based Olink platform (r = 0.95) (Pietzner et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pietzner et al., 2021b

claim: Genetic estimates on adulthood circulating leptin levels were obtained from 35,559 individuals enrolled in the deCODE Health study (mean age: 55 y, SD: 17 y).
source: We also obtained genetic estimates on adulthood circulating leptin levels from a previously conducted large-scale study of 35,559 individuals enrolled in the deCODE Health study (mean age: 55 y, SD: 17 y).
evidence: Description of data source

claim: Childhood adiposity has a total effect on circulating leptin at age 10 y (β = 1.28 SD change in leptin levels per change in body size category, 95% CI = 1.10–1.46, p=2 × 10–41).
source: We firstly conducted univariable MR to estimate the total effect of childhood adiposity on circulating leptin using data measured in ALSPAC participants at mean age 9.9 y in the lifecourse (β = 1.28 SD change in leptin levels per change in body size category, 95% CI = 1.10–1.46, p=2 × 10–41).
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results from ALSPAC data

claim: Childhood body size has a direct effect on increased leptin levels at age 10 y (β = 1.10, 95% CI = 0.90–1.30, p=6 × 10–28).
source: This was followed by applying multivariable MR, which provided evidence that childhood body size has a direct effect on increased leptin levels at this point in the lifecourse (β = 1.10, 95% CI = 0.90–1.30, p=6 × 10–28) (Figure 1A and B, Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: Childhood adiposity has a total effect on circulating leptin measured in adulthood (β = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36–0.61, p=5 × 10–14).
source: Both childhood and adult adiposity likewise provided evidence of a total effect on circulating leptin measured in adulthood (β = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36–0.61, p=5 × 10–14 and β = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.49–0,69, p=2 × 10–32, respectively) (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: Adult adiposity has a total effect on circulating leptin measured in adulthood (β = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.49–0.69, p=2 × 10–32).
source: Both childhood and adult adiposity likewise provided evidence of a total effect on circulating leptin measured in adulthood (β = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.36–0.61, p=5 × 10–14 and β = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.49–0,69, p=2 × 10–32, respectively) (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: Childhood adiposity indirectly influences leptin levels measured during adulthood along the causal pathway involving adult body size (β = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.42–0.69, p=1 × 10–15).
source: However, multivariable MR analyses suggested that childhood adiposity indirectly influences leptin levels measured during adulthood along the causal pathway involving adult body size (β = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.42–0.69, p=1 × 10–15) (Figure 1C and D, Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 1C and D

claim: Adipose tissue-derived BMI has a total effect on leptin levels measured during childhood (β = 0.61, 95% CI = 0.13–1.08, p=0.01).
source: Univariable MR analyses provided evidence of a total effect of adiposity on leptin levels measured during childhood based on analyses using the adipose tissue (β = 0.61, 95% CI = 0.13–1.08, p=0.01) and brain tissue (β = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.40–1.31, p=2 × 10–4) partitioned instruments.
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: Brain tissue-derived BMI has a total effect on leptin levels measured during childhood (β = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.40–1.31, p=2 × 10–4).
source: Univariable MR analyses provided evidence of a total effect of adiposity on leptin levels measured during childhood based on analyses using the adipose tissue (β = 0.61, 95% CI = 0.13–1.08, p=0.01) and brain tissue (β = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.40–1.31, p=2 × 10–4) partitioned instruments.
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: The brain tissue-derived component of BMI predominates in the effect on childhood leptin levels (β = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.22–1.36, p=6 × 10–3).
source: In a multivariable setting, the brain tissue-derived component of BMI predominated in the model (β = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.22–1.36, p=6 × 10–3), whereas the adipose tissue-derived estimate attenuated to include the null (β = 0.12, 95% CI = −0.48–0.71, p=0.70) (Figure 2A and B, Supplementary file 1h).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: The adipose tissue-derived estimate for childhood leptin attenuated to include the null in multivariable analysis (β = 0.12, 95% CI = −0.48–0.71, p=0.70).
source: In a multivariable setting, the brain tissue-derived component of BMI predominated in the model (β = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.22–1.36, p=6 × 10–3), whereas the adipose tissue-derived estimate attenuated to include the null (β = 0.12, 95% CI = −0.48–0.71, p=0.70) (Figure 2A and B, Supplementary file 1h).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: Adipose tissue-derived BMI has a total effect on adulthood measured leptin (β = 0.39, 95% CI = 0.21–0.57, p=3 × 10–5).
source: Analyses on adulthood measured leptin also provided strong evidence of a total effect based on adipose-and brain tissue-derived estimates (β = 0.39, 95% CI = 0.21–0.57, p=3 × 10–5 and β = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.28–0.56, p=2 × 10–9, respectively).
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: Brain tissue-derived BMI has a total effect on adulthood measured leptin (β = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.28–0.56, p=2 × 10–9).
source: Analyses on adulthood measured leptin also provided strong evidence of a total effect based on adipose-and brain tissue-derived estimates (β = 0.39, 95% CI = 0.21–0.57, p=3 × 10–5 and β = 0.42, 95% CI = 0.28–0.56, p=2 × 10–9, respectively).
evidence: Univariable MR analysis results

claim: Subcutaneous adipose tissue-derived BMI estimates attenuated substantially in multivariable analysis of adulthood leptin (β = 0.14, 95% CI = −0.14–0.42, p=0.33).
source: Similar to findings for childhood leptin, subcutaneous adipose tissue-derived estimates attenuated substantially more (β = 0.14, 95% CI = −0.14–0.42, p=0.33) compared to the estimates derived using the brain tissue instrument set (β = 0.38, 95% CI = 0.14–0.62, p=2 × 10–3) in a multivariable setting (Figure 2C and D, Supplementary file 1i and j).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 2C and D

claim: Brain tissue-derived BMI estimates remained robust in multivariable analysis of adulthood leptin (β = 0.38, 95% CI = 0.14–0.62, p=2 × 10–3).
source: Similar to findings for childhood leptin, subcutaneous adipose tissue-derived estimates attenuated substantially more (β = 0.14, 95% CI = −0.14–0.42, p=0.33) compared to the estimates derived using the brain tissue instrument set (β = 0.38, 95% CI = 0.14–0.62, p=2 × 10–3) in a multivariable setting (Figure 2C and D, Supplementary file 1i and j).
evidence: Multivariable MR analysis results shown in Figure 2C and D

claim: Brain-expressed BMI instruments have a predominating effect on visceral fat volume (β = 0.51, 95% CI = 0.30–0.72, p=2 × 10–6).
source: As a further sensitivity analysis to characterize the causal pathway between these tissue-partitioned variants and fat distribution, we found that in particular the brain-expressed instruments have a predominating effect on visceral fat volume (β = 0.51, 95% CI = 0.30–0.72, p=2 × 10–6) compared to the subcutaneous adipose instruments (β = 0.07, 95% CI = −0.18–0.32, p=0.57) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1m).
evidence: Sensitivity analysis results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Subcutaneous adipose BMI instruments have a minimal effect on visceral fat volume (β = 0.07, 95% CI = −0.18–0.32, p=0.57).
source: As a further sensitivity analysis to characterize the causal pathway between these tissue-partitioned variants and fat distribution, we found that in particular the brain-expressed instruments have a predominating effect on visceral fat volume (β = 0.51, 95% CI = 0.30–0.72, p=2 × 10–6) compared to the subcutaneous adipose instruments (β = 0.07, 95% CI = −0.18–0.32, p=0.57) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1m).
evidence: Sensitivity analysis results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Adiposity in childhood exerts a direct effect on leptin levels when measured in early life.
source: Our application of lifecourse MR in this work supports a breadth of previous research using this technique, which highlights the importance of taking into consideration the age at which data from participants for exposure and outcome datasets are analyzed. Findings from this study provide evidence that adiposity in childhood exerts a direct effect on leptin levels when measured in early life, corroborating findings from observational studies (Shalitin and Phillip, 2003).
evidence: Supported by MR analysis results and citation to observational studies

claim: Childhood adiposity has an indirect effect on leptin measured in later life along the causal pathway involving adulthood adiposity.
source: Conversely, evidence of an indirect effect along the causal pathway involving adulthood adiposity was found when analyzing leptin measured in later life.
evidence: Based on MR analysis results presented earlier

claim: Lifecourse MR has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on lower risk of breast cancer.
source: This provides a powerful proof of concept for this approach, which has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on lower risk of breast cancer (Richardson et al., 2020), elevated risk of type 1 diabetes (Richardson et al., 2022a), and an influence on cardiac structure (O'Nunain et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Richardson et al., 2020

claim: Lifecourse MR has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on elevated risk of type 1 diabetes.
source: This provides a powerful proof of concept for this approach, which has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on lower risk of breast cancer (Richardson et al., 2020), elevated risk of type 1 diabetes (Richardson et al., 2022a), and an influence on cardiac structure (O'Nunain et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Richardson et al., 2022a

claim: Lifecourse MR has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on cardiac structure.
source: This provides a powerful proof of concept for this approach, which has previously found evidence of a direct effect of increased childhood adiposity on lower risk of breast cancer (Richardson et al., 2020), elevated risk of type 1 diabetes (Richardson et al., 2022a), and an influence on cardiac structure (O'Nunain et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Nunain et al., 2022

claim: The subcomponent of BMI proxied using genetic variants whose effects are putatively mediated via gene expression in brain tissue are predominantly responsible for driving effects of adiposity on leptin during both childhood and adulthood.
source: Tissue-partitioned MR analyses in this work suggest that the subcomponent of BMI proxied using genetic variants whose effects are putatively mediated via gene expression in brain tissue are predominantly responsible for driving effects of adiposity on leptin during both childhood and adulthood.
evidence: Based on tissue-partitioned MR analysis results presented earlier

claim: These findings highlight a role for appetite regulation and energy expenditure mechanisms as of fundamental importance in the effect of adiposity on leptin levels.
source: We postulate that these findings highlight a role for appetite regulation and energy expenditure mechanisms as of fundamental importance in the effect of adiposity on leptin levels.
evidence: Authors' interpretation of their findings

claim: Being overweight has a downstream consequence on elevated leptin levels due to leptin resistance occurring in the central nervous system, particularly the hypothalamus.
source: This corroborates findings from the literature, which suggest that being overweight has a downstream consequence on elevated leptin levels due to leptin resistance occurring in the central nervous system, particularly the hypothalamus (Gruzdeva et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gruzdeva et al., 2019

claim: Leptin resistance is influenced by factors such as blood–brain barrier permeability, which results in leptin failing to suppress appetite and consequently leads to circulating hyperleptinemia amongst patients with obesity.
source: This is influenced by factors such as blood–brain barrier permeability, which results in leptin failing to suppress appetite and consequently leads to circulating hyperleptinemia amongst patients with obesity (Izquierdo et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Izquierdo et al., 2019

claim: Leptin may have long-term consequences for appetite suppression that influences excess body weight starting in childhood and sustained into later life.
source: Taken together with the evidence of an indirect effect highlighted by our lifecourse MR analysis, these findings suggest that leptin may have long-term consequences for appetite suppression. This in turn has an influence on excess body weight, which may start in childhood and then can be sustained into later life.
evidence: Authors' interpretation combining their findings with literature

claim: Leptin is primarily produced in subcutaneous adipose tissues.
source: Future research in this space should investigate large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) outcomes related to subcutaneous adipose tissues (e.g. skinfold thickness), particularly given that this is where leptin is primarily produced (Russell et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Russell et al., 1998

claim: The manner in which adipose- and brain tissue-partitioned BMI instruments relate to downstream disease and complex traits can drastically differ despite having almost identical average effect estimates on BMI.
source: For the adipose- and brain tissue-partitioned sets of instruments used in this study, we found previously that the manner in which they relate to downstream disease and complex traits can drastically differ despite having almost identical average effect estimates on BMI as an exposure.
evidence: Based on previous findings from the authors' work

claim: Brain tissue-derived BMI variants are predominantly responsible for the effect of BMI on both cigarette smoking and lung cancer.
source: For example, we previously found evidence that the brain tissue-derived variants are predominantly responsible for the effect of BMI on both cigarette smoking and lung cancer (Leyden et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Leyden et al., 2023

claim: BMI likely captures various causal pathways underlying the relationship between anthropometry and complex outcomes.
source: In particular, this finding underlines the heterogeneous nature of BMI as a lifestyle risk factor and highlights that this human-derived construct likely captures various causal pathways underlying the relationship between anthropometry and complex outcomes.
evidence: Authors' interpretation based on their findings

claim: The childhood and adult body size instruments do not provide insight into other timepoints over the lifecourse (e.g. adolescence).
source: For instance, the childhood and adult body size instruments used to disentangle direct and indirect effects in this study do not provide insight into other timepoints over the lifecourse (e.g. adolescence).
evidence: Authors' acknowledgment of study limitations

claim: The childhood adiposity instruments are based on recall data.
source: Moreover, the childhood adiposity instruments are based on recall data, which is why they required validation in three independent cohorts as described in the 'Methods' section.
evidence: Description of instrument derivation methodology

claim: Tissue-partitioned instruments were derived using bulk tissue and do not take into account cell-type heterogeneity.
source: In addition, tissue-partitioned instruments were derived using bulk tissue in this work due to the availability of data and therefore do not take into account cell-type heterogeneity (Glastonbury et al., 2019; Prince et al., 2021).
evidence: Authors' acknowledgment of methodological limitation with supporting citations

claim: The findings highlight a putative role for genes expressed in neural tissues in the etiology of adiposity and leptin levels during both childhood and adulthood.
source: In summary, our findings highlight a putative role for genes expressed in neural tissues in the etiology of adiposity and leptin levels during both childhood and adulthood.
evidence: Authors' summary of their findings

claim: This study provides a proof of concept into how the principles of MR can be adapted to investigate hypotheses outside the scope of how this causal inference technique was originally conceived.
source: Furthermore, this innovative study provides a proof of concept into how the principles of MR can be adapted to investigate the hypotheses outside the scope of how this causal inference technique was originally conceived (Davey Smith and Ebrahim, 2003).
evidence: Authors' interpretation of the methodological contribution with citation to original MR conception
